[[Bengaluru]], often referred to as the technology capital of [[India]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Elizabeth |first=Shilpa |date=2024-07-08 |title=From electricity to Electronics City: Tracing Bengaluru's journey to becoming the tech capital |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/bangalore/from-electricity-to-electronic-city-tracing-bengalurus-journey-to-becoming-the-tech-capital/article68363114.ece |access-date=2025-06-24 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> is experiencing a significant boom in [[Tower block|high-rise]] construction.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=2025-03-03 |title=Bengaluru's 60% FAR increase to drive high-rise growth, but experts warn of strain on crumbling infrastructure |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/real-estate/bengalurus-60-far-increase-to-drive-high-rise-growth-but-experts-warn-of-strain-on-crumbling-infrastructure-101740810091219.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250406074321/https://www.hindustantimes.com/real-estate/bengalurus-60-far-increase-to-drive-high-rise-growth-but-experts-warn-of-strain-on-crumbling-infrastructure-101740810091219.html |archive-date=2025-04-06 |access-date=2025-06-24 |work=Hindustan Times |language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Under-Construction Luxury Housing Sees 55% YoY Price Growth |url=https://www.rprealtyplus.com/newsviews/under-construction-luxury-housing-sees-55-yoy-price-growth-118211.html |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=Realty Plus Magazine |language=en}}</ref> The city has emerged as one of the [[List of largest cities|fastest-growing cities globally]],<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-10-23 |title=Top 10 fastest-developing cities in the world |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/etimes/trending/10-ten-fastest-developing-cities-in-the-world/photostory/114473598.cms |access-date=2025-06-24 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> attracting a highly skilled workforce from across the country seeking employment and business opportunities. This rapid urban growth has led to a sustained demand for both [[Residential area|residential]] and [[Commercial area|commercial]] real estate, prompting a shift towards vertical development.<ref name=":1" />  

The tallest building in Bengaluru is the CNTC Presidential Tower, which [[topping out|topped out]] in early 2023. Standing at {{convert|161|m|ft|0}} with 50 floors, it is also the tallest building in the [[States and union territories of India|state]] of [[Karnataka]] and was the 11th-tallest in [[South India]] at the time of its completion.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tower |first=The Presidential |title=Bengaluru's Tallest - The Presidential Tower turns pink to celebrate women across the world |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/in/news-releases/bengalurus-tallest---the-presidential-tower-turns-pink-to-celebrate-women-across-the-world-301768765.html |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=prnewswire.com |language=en}}</ref> The tallest commercial building is the [[World Trade Center Bangalore|World Trade Center]], which was completed in 2010 and rises to {{convert|128|m|ft|0}} with 32 floors.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |date=2010-08-25 |title=World Trade Centre in Bangalore |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/bangalore/World-Trade-Centre-in-Bangalore/article16144574.ece |access-date=2025-06-24 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> 

Other notable high-rises in the city include [[UB City|UB Tower]], Mantri DSK Pinnacle, and Phoenix One Bangalore West.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dhamija |first=Anshul |date=2011-10-23 |title=Vijay Mallya's White House in the sky: First-ever visuals & details |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/vijay-mallyas-white-house-in-the-sky-first-ever-visuals-details/articleshow/10387503.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-06-24 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=13 July 2021 |title=Phoenix's One Bangalore West announces the launch of its new skyline homes |url=https://www.business-standard.com/content/press-releases-ani/phoenix-s-one-bangalore-west-announces-the-launch-of-its-new-skyline-homes-121071300728_1.html |work=Business Standard}}</ref> Among the tallest skyscrapers currently under construction are the four towers of Codename Peaklife project, each projected to reach a height of {{convert|231|m|ft|0}}.{{Citation needed|date=June 2025}}

== History ==
The first [[Tower block|high-rise]] building in [[Bengaluru]] over {{convert|100|m|ft|0}} was the [[Public Utility Building, Bengaluru|Public Utility Building]] on [[M G Road, Bengaluru|M.G. Road]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=T.R |first=Jahnavi |date=2022-05-29 |title=Height of neglect: Bengaluru's Public Utility Building a shadow of its former self |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/bangalore/few-give-one-of-bengalurus-oldest-skyscraper-a-second-look/article65440357.ece |access-date=2025-06-24 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> Standing at {{convert|106|m|ft|0}} with 25 floors, it was the [[List of tallest buildings in India|tallest building in India]] at the time of its completion in 1973 before being surpassed by the [[World Trade Centre, Mumbai|World Trade Centre Mumbai]] in 1974. The Public Utility Building was only the second building in India to surpass a height of {{convert|100|m|ft|0}} and remained a dominant feature of Bengaluru's skyline for decades. The building housed [[Office|offices]], [[Retail format|retail outlets]], and a [[hotel]], and served as an early example of vertical [[mixed-use development]] in the country.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tale of Utility Building now turns a story of futility |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/content/315676/tale-utility-building-now-turns.html |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref>

=== Late 20th century: Early developments ===
Bengaluru's ascent as a technology centre began in the 1980s and 1990s with the establishment of major [[Science park|IT parks]] like [[Electronic City]] and [[Whitefield, Bengaluru|Whitefield]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'DeaJanuary |first=Christopher |date=February 2016 |title=Bangalore: Electronic city |url=https://realassets.ipe.com/asia-pacific/bangalore-electronic-city/10011826.article |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=Real Assets |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> Early high-rises were limited, primarily [[Low-rise building|low-rise]] and mid-rise office buildings, due to [[Zoning|regulatory constraints]] and proximity to the [[HAL Airport]], which was located in the heart of the city and served as the city's only [[airport]] until 2008.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Moodie |first=Martin |date=2008-05-25 |title=Take-off time in Bangalore: Bengaluru International Airport gets away to historic, satisfactory start-up – 26/05/08 |url=https://moodiedavittreport.com/take-off-time-in-bangalore-bengaluru-international-airport-gets-away-to-historic-satisfactory-start-up-260508/ |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=Moodie Davitt Report |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== 2000s: Policy reforms and rise in vertical development ===
The [[Bangalore Development Authority]] (BDA) and the newly-formed [[Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike]] (BBMP) relaxed the [[Floor area ratio|floor area ratio (FAR)]] norms in the 2000s, particularly in newly planned zones like the [[Outer Ring Road, Bengaluru|Outer Ring Road]] and [[Bengaluru|North Bengaluru]].<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Khan |first1=Sobia |last2=Nair |first2=Athira |date=2015-03-04 |title=Bengaluru allows helipads atop 20 high-rise buildings, residential towers |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/infrastructure/bengaluru-allows-helipads-atop-20-high-rise-buildings-residential-towers/articleshow/46452508.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-06-24 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> Moreover, with the inauguration of the [[Kempegowda International Airport]] in 2008 and cessation of [[Commercial aviation|commercial flight]] operation at the HAL Airport in May 2008, the height restrictions in several parts of the city were relaxed.<ref name=":3" /> This resulted in a surge of mid-rise construction across both residential and commercial use. The late 2000s witnessed the completion of several iconic [[Tower block|high-rises]] like the Canberra Tower, Concorde Tower, and UB Tower, all of which were completed within the [[UB City|UB City complex]] in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |last2= |last3= |first3= |date=21 October 2008 |title=Sophistication steps into town |url=https://bangaloremirror.indiatimes.com/entertainment/lounge/sophistication-steps-into-town/articleshow/22379079.cms |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=Bangalore Mirror |language=en}}</ref> At {{convert|123|m|ft|0}} in height, [[UB City|UB Tower]] surpassed the Public Utility Building, which had remained the tallest building in Bengaluru for 35 years.
[[File:View from Visvesvaraya Industrial and Technological Museum (2025) 02.jpg|thumb|263x263px|[[Bengaluru|Bengaluru's]] skyline viewed from Central Business District]]

=== 2010s–2020s: Skyscraper era ===
The completion of the [[World Trade Center Bengaluru|World Trade Center]] in 2010 (128m, 32 floors) signaled strong momentum towards vertical development in the city. The [[UB City|UB Tower]] and the [[World Trade Center Bengaluru|World Trade Center]] were among the first glass-clad high-rises in the city and set a design template for subsequent development.<ref name=":2" /> A combination of soaring demand, scarcity of land within key [[Central business district|business districts]], and rising office prices accelerated construction of high-rise buildings.<ref>{{Cite news |date=14 April 2025 |title=CREDAI Bengaluru recommendations seek government action for sustainable urban growth |url=https://www.constructionweekonline.in/business/credai-bengaluru-recommendations |work=Construction Week}}</ref> Mantri DSK Pinnacle, which was also the tallest building in South India when it topped out in 2013 at {{convert|153|m|ft|0}}, marked Bengaluru's entry into the [[skyscraper]] era.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2012-08-10 |title=Mantri Pinnacle-Ultra luxurious and tallest residential tower in South India |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/mantri-pinnacle-ultra-luxurious-and-tallest-residential-tower-in-south-india/articleshow/15405572.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-06-24 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2014-06-13 |title=Looking up to the sky |url=https://www.thehindu.com/features/homes-and-gardens/looking-up-to-the-sky/article6111768.ece |access-date=2025-06-24 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

Several residential and mixed-use [[Megaproject|mega projects]] are under construction in emerging suburbs along transit corridors and [[Satellite city|satellite towns]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Datta |first=Souptik |date=28 March 2025 |title=Bengaluru real estate: Is Devanahalli the IT capital's Gurugram in the making? |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/real-estate/bengaluru-real-estate-is-devanahalli-the-it-capital-s-gurugram-in-the-making-101743083075788.html |work=Hindustan Times}}</ref> As of 2025, over 1,500<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bangalore high-rises |url=https://www.emporis.com/city/100247/bangalore-india |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151003033505/http://www.emporis.com/city/100247/bangalore-india |archive-date=3 October 2015}}</ref> high-rise buildings dot the [[Metropolitan area|metropolitan region]], and that number continues to grow, signifying the city's sustained push toward vertical expansion.

extract:
Bengaluru, often referred to as the technology capital of India, is experiencing a significant boom in high-rise construction. The city has emerged as one of the fastest-growing cities globally, attracting a highly skilled workforce from across the country seeking employment and business opportunities. This rapid urban growth has led to a sustained demand for both residential and commercial real estate, prompting a shift towards vertical development.  
The tallest building in Bengaluru is the CNTC Presidential Tower, which topped out in early 2023. Standing at 161 metres (528 ft) with 50 floors, it is also the tallest building in the state of Karnataka and was the 11th-tallest in South India at the time of its completion. The tallest commercial building is the World Trade Center, which was completed in 2010 and rises to 128 metres (420 ft) with 32 floors. 
Other notable high-rises in the city include UB Tower, Mantri DSK Pinnacle, and Phoenix One Bangalore West. Among the tallest skyscrapers currently under construction are the four towers of Codename Peaklife project, each projected to reach a height of 231 metres (758 ft).
